name: PointCast
summary: In a 3D particle cloud on a 2D screen, a single click sends a ray into the data; the system reads the density along the ray and selects the first real cluster it passes through, skipping faint ones.
howItWorks: The density field is sampled along the ray through the clicked point, and stretches above 10% of the maximum are treated as clusters. The nearest one is selected unless its accumulated density is under 10% of the strongest, in which case the strongest is taken. The selection is grown from that point with a threshold of 20% of its peak density, and lowering the threshold afterwards reveals how the cluster connects to others. Participants preferred it most, especially for partly occluded clusters, since only a small visible part is needed. Compared on a pen tablet (20 participants) with cylinder selection and CloudLasso: the CAST techniques took 16 to 23 s against 43 s for CloudLasso and 88 s for cylinders, with the same accuracy.
